profile: Browser Wasm profiles: Swink and its native remote-lisp clients are omitted modules
rationale: The user clarified that Swink will not be used in the browser. Account for its native-baseline presence and exclude the complete module/client surface from browser packaging. This creates no Swink port, replacement server or host-service deliverable.
required_integration: Keep all native compilation, loading and binding witnesses in the native census.
Record the browser module exclusion for SWINK, remote-lisp and the Cocoa remote client; include all resident and later-loaded module bindings.
Check that the required browser startup closure does not rely on an excluded module; preserve any genuinely shared Lisp dependency under its own supported contract.
If a supported browser entry can request an excluded module, use and test the shared module loader unsupported-module condition. Do not create a Swink-specific runtime, socket stub, server or client.
Do not add a TCP debugger, Swink compatibility layer or new host-service requirement to the plan.
limitations: This is a browser packaging and dependency-scope decision, not a native baseline change or applied graph disposition.
All module bindings are covered by the scope decision; package membership alone does not prove a function body is a socket operation.
The browser startup dependency check remains open. Exclusion alone gives no census credit.
General Lisp threads, streams, CLOS and mailbox-based debugger services retain their own contracts.

scope_clarification.user_words: You know we won't use swink in the browser, right?

binding_coverage: The exclusion applies to the whole module and all resident/later binding versions, including the 25 resident unannotated prototypes identified in Claude audit 51. The recorded READ-SEXP installation is an example, not the module boundary.
